about: ChitBridge country comparison of accounting packages, one flat rows[] list like compat.json so the Standards page can load it into CBList. status: ahead|level|behind|n/a. checked (per row): the date the row was last held against its source; source_url: the first official page in source. verified: source = the claim is in the cited source (for India, 2026-10-24: every theirs read on the vendor's own help or pricing page, every ours read in our code); memory = the cited doc says 'from knowledge' or the sources are silent, check before external use. Not covered: Busy, Marg, Odoo, FTA-accredited UAE packs (no source in docs), and any UAE VAT, bank, multi-currency or inventory claim. Rows are left out where sources say nothing. The ours column is as built on 2026-10-15 (AU1 and CA1/CA2 are queued, not built).

rows.theirs: Balance sheet, profit and loss, trial balance, day book, ledgers and cash flow.
rows.ours: Double-entry books with balance sheet, profit and loss and trial balance. An entry is reversed, never edited; a closed month is locked.

rows.theirs: GSTR-1 is filed from TallyPrime itself with EVC or DSC (Release 5.0). GSTR-3B is downloaded, reconciled and uploaded from TallyPrime, then filed and paid on the GST portal.
rows.ours: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are prepared from the posted books, ready to upload. Nothing is filed from here yet.

rows.theirs: The IRN is generated from the sales entry through Tally’s own GSP; the invoice prints with the IRN and QR code; bulk generation too.
rows.ours: The e-invoice (IRN) file is built from the invoice and checked before anyone sends it. No connection to the e-invoice portal yet, so nothing is sent from here.

rows.theirs: Bank statements in Excel, CSV or MT940 are imported and matched automatically (Release 6.0, 145 or more banks). With Connected Banking some banks’ statements arrive directly.
rows.ours: A bank statement file (CSV or JSON) is read and matched to the books and to payments already on the rail. Every suggestion is confirmed by a person; nothing posts itself. No live bank link.
rows.better: A payment already on the rail explains its statement line before anyone types.

rows.theirs: A base currency plus any foreign currencies, exchange rates by date, forex gain or loss worked out automatically.
rows.ours: One currency per shop, fixed when the shop starts. No foreign-currency entries, no revaluation.

rows.theirs: An Edit Log records every change and deletion of a voucher (and of ledgers, stock items and groups). In the Edit Log edition it cannot be switched off; in the regular edition it can.
rows.ours: The books only ever add a line: an entry is reversed, never changed or deleted. Every entry names the rule version it was posted under, and the period pack is sealed with a checksum.
rows.better: Nothing to switch on or off: a change is impossible, not merely logged.

rows.theirs: A supplier’s invoice can arrive over Bharat Connect and be accepted into a purchase entry, and payment details go back the same way. Otherwise the buyer keys the supplier’s invoice in. Each side keeps its own copy.
rows.ours: Buyer and seller hold the same sealed chit. It is matched to the order and the receipt, and a dispute is a thread on the line, not an e-mail chase.
rows.better: One record for both parties, not two copies exchanged.

rows.theirs: Masters and vouchers move in and out as XML or JSON files, or in from Excel with a column map. Bank transactions cannot be imported from Excel.
rows.ours: We read your stock items and company details from Tally over its XML port and send each sale and receipt to Tally as a voucher; the month’s entries can be written as Tally files. Tested on a real TallyPrime for stock items and a receipt; sales vouchers tested on a stand-in so far. Your Tally trial balance can be read beside ours from an export file. Not yet: moving your whole Tally books into ChitBridge.

rows.theirs: Profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow reports; bank reconciliation and GST reports on every plan, the Free plan included.
rows.ours: Double-entry books with balance sheet, profit and loss and trial balance. An entry is reversed, never edited; a closed month is locked.

rows.theirs: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are pushed to the GST portal from Zoho Books (Zoho is a GSP). GSTR-1 can be filed from Zoho Books or on the portal; GSTR-3B is filed and paid on the portal.
rows.ours: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are prepared from the posted books, ready to upload. Nothing is filed from here yet.

rows.theirs: Invoices go straight to the e-invoice portal through Zoho’s own GSP and come back with the IRN and QR code. On every paid plan from Standard.
rows.ours: The e-invoice (IRN) file is built from the invoice and checked before anyone sends it. No connection to the e-invoice portal yet, so nothing is sent from here.

rows.theirs: Automatic bank feeds through Yodlee or Token for supported banks, up to 90 days back; statements in CSV, TSV, OFX, QIF, CAMT.053 or PDF can be imported; matching with rules.
rows.ours: A bank statement file (CSV or JSON) is read and matched to the books and to payments already on the rail. Every suggestion is confirmed by a person; nothing posts itself. No live bank link.
rows.better: A payment already on the rail explains its statement line before anyone types.

rows.theirs: Transactions in other currencies from the Professional plan; exchange rates fetched automatically or typed by hand.
rows.ours: One currency per shop, fixed when the shop starts. No foreign-currency entries, no revaluation.

rows.theirs: An activity log and audit trail keep every version of a transaction, with who changed what and when. No user or admin can change the log.
rows.ours: The books only ever add a line: an entry is reversed, never changed or deleted. Every entry names the rule version it was posted under, and the period pack is sealed with a checksum.
rows.better: Nothing to switch on or off: a change is impossible, not merely logged.

rows.theirs: A vendor portal: your vendor accepts or declines your purchase order and uploads a bill as a PDF or image (5 MB), which you accept into a bill. The portal is a shared window; each side keeps its own books.
rows.ours: Buyer and seller hold the same sealed chit. It is matched to the order and the receipt, and a dispute is a thread on the line, not an e-mail chase.
rows.better: One record for both parties, not two copies exchanged.

rows.theirs: Invoices, bills, items and contacts import from CSV, TSV or XLS files (10 MB). A REST API with OAuth covers every module: 100 calls a minute, 1,000 a day on Free.
rows.ours: Our connector reads your items from Zoho Books through its API and can send sales invoices and payments to it. Written from Zoho’s published API and tested on a stand-in, not yet on a live Zoho organisation. Not yet: moving your Zoho books into ChitBridge.
